::: {.bnr-manual-flag .bnr-manual-flag--operations}
Operations Manual
:::

**Owner:** BNR Lead and BNR Analyst.

## Purpose

Use this page when a published result, report or website page needs correcting. The aim is to correct the problem openly, keep a clear record of what happened, and make sure that corrected results go through the same checks as the original release.

Do not edit a generated dataset, receipt or published analytical file by hand to make it look correct.

## Step 1: Understand the problem

1. Record what was found, who found it and the date.
2. Record which release, files, report or website pages may be affected.
3. Decide where the problem began:

   | If the problem is in… | Start by checking… |
   |---|---|
   | The original information | The source system or controlled source dataset |
   | A calculation or automated rule | The approved Stata code or configuration |
   | The wording or interpretation of an approved result | The Quarto page or report text |
   | Spelling, layout or a broken website link | The Quarto page |

4. Decide whether the problem could affect published numbers, conclusions, confidentiality or people who use the information.
5. If confidential information may have become public, tell the BNR Lead immediately and follow the approved incident process.

Keep a short private note explaining what was found and why a correction is needed.

## Step 2: Correct the earliest affected point

Correct the problem at its source wherever possible.

For example:

- correct a source-data problem in the controlled source data, then rerun the affected workflow;
- correct a calculation problem in the version-controlled Stata code, then rerun the affected workflow;
- correct a wording or layout problem in the Quarto source, then render the website again.

Do not change a later file if an earlier source, calculation or rule is the real cause.

## Step 3: Rebuild and review the affected release

Start again from the earliest workflow step affected by the correction.

1. Run the relevant workflow using its normal controlled process.
2. Review the regenerated outputs and checks.
3. Complete disclosure review again if published statistics have changed.
4. Obtain a new approval where the workflow requires it.
5. Publish the corrected approved package through the normal Stata publication step.
6. Check both the authoritative public package and its website copy.

Use the relevant workflow guide:

- [CVD events](../post-redcap/cvd-events-workflow.qmd)
- [CVD mortality](../post-redcap/mortality-workflow.qmd)
- [Rolling monthly update](../post-redcap/rolling-update.qmd)
- [Annual report](../post-redcap/annual-report.qmd)
- [One-off report](../post-redcap/one-off-report.qmd)

Then refresh any affected [dashboards](../post-redcap/dashboard-regeneration.qmd), [tables](../post-redcap/tabulation-regeneration.qmd), [Downloads page](../post-redcap/downloads-page-regeneration.qmd) or [report listings](../post-redcap/report-listings-regeneration.qmd).

## Step 4: Update the website

1. Update any affected Quarto wording, links, listings or correction note.
2. Add a clear public correction note if readers need to understand a material change.
3. Preview the affected pages and run a complete local Quarto render.
4. Check that the corrected pages match the approved public package.
5. Review the changed files in VS Code Source Control.
6. Commit and push the correction to a working branch.
7. Create a pull request on GitHub and merge it into `main` only when the change is ready.
8. Check GitHub Actions and the live website after the merge.

See [Render and publish the website](../../technical/website/render-publish.qmd) for the detailed branch, pull-request and GitHub Actions process.

## Keep a clear history

Keep:

- the earlier authoritative package;
- the corrected replacement;
- a private note explaining what changed and why;
- the new approval and publication records; and
- any public correction note or communication.

This makes it possible to understand which version was used at any point and why it was replaced.

::: {.callout-warning title="BNR confirmation required"}

BNR should agree and record:

- who can order an urgent withdrawal from the public website;
- where superseded packages are kept;
- when a public correction note is needed; and
- how affected data users are told about a material correction.

:::
